what_this_round_is: an independent REPRODUCTION of the r3 design trade-off, so that the substance behind the dangling r3_fix_record.md reference is readable without substituting for it
what_this_round_is_not: an acceptance, an approval, or a status transition
a signature on behalf of any other party

authority.note: no owner ruling was needed: this round measures and registers, and writes nothing into the attempt

trigger: Round 68 found F-R68-01: the r3 comment block in observability.py says 'see r3_fix_record.md' and that file does not exist.

the_decision_this_round_makes_explicit.decision: r3_fix_record.md is NOT written by the orchestrator
the_decision_this_round_makes_explicit.reason: a dangling reference is EXPLICITLY BROKEN -- the reader knows the record is absent and goes looking. A substitute looks authoritative but is not the document the author meant, so downstream readers cite it as the original and the hole is permanently covered.
the_decision_this_round_makes_explicit.generalisation: filling a missing carrier is only safe when the carrier is reconstructible FROM MEASUREMENT. When it is not, leaving the hole and supplying the substance is better than manufacturing a plausible stand-in.
the_decision_this_round_makes_explicit.what_is_supplied_instead: an independent reproduction of the trade-off, runnable by anyone

measurement.method: rebind observability._AUTH_PATTERN in memory to each candidate, exactly as the attempt's own scratch scripts did, then measure against the CURRENT 28-case oracle, the CURRENT 79-row rule table, and the r2 reviewer's C1-C12 matrix

builder_faithfulness.question: is the pattern builder faithful?
builder_faithfulness.test: feed it the product's OWN _AUTH_SCHEME_SPLIT and require it to rebuild the product's OWN _AUTH_PATTERN byte for byte
builder_faithfulness.why_it_was_needed: the first version re-typed the RFC-7235 token class and the tails as literals; the resulting string differed from the landed one by a few characters, so that reproduction measured a pattern that is NOT the pattern on disk. Fixed by using the module's own constant and asserting faithfulness separately.

the_comment_blocks_claim_is_reproduced.claim: closing the two-token-then-wrap shape needs the scheme's own line consumed as a token run, which deletes doc=17
the_comment_blocks_claim_is_reproduced.over_redaction_measured: Authorization: Bearer newline doc=17 becomes Authorization: <redacted>, i.e. doc=17 is deleted

but_the_cost_must_be_classified_before_i.why: four failures appear (2 oracle + 2 rule), and they are NOT all the same kind. Two of them ARE the registered-open rows: R3a-two-token-then-wrap and open-two-token-then-wrap assert the residual output exactly, so closing the leak turns them red because the registration is working, not because a defect appeared.
but_the_cost_must_be_classified_before_i.consequence: counting all four as 'the cost' overstates it; the real cost is 2 over-redaction regressions plus 2 rows to re-register

F-R69-01.what: all ten of the attempt's own design-exploration scratch scripts are now unrunnable
F-R69-01.cause: they unpack oracle.CASES as a 6-tuple; the r3 iteration widened it to 7 (..., expect_len, declared_residual)
F-R69-01.error: ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 6)
F-R69-01.disposition: not edited (they are attempt artefacts and editing them changes their hashes); this round re-implements the measurement instead
F-R69-01.generalisation: a script is a fossil of the interface it was written against. When the interface moves, everything under scratch/ breaks at once and nobody is notified. 'It ran then' and 'it still runs' are two different claims.

the_three_register_items_collapse_into_o.measurement: oracle.md (f188e853...), fix_record.md (68fb5800...) and binding.json (5fd462c9...) all have their hashes registered in after/final_hashes.json
the_three_register_items_collapse_into_o.consequence: ANY correction to them -- append-only included -- necessarily changes their hashes, so the three documentary corrections cannot land inside the r2 generation
the_three_register_items_collapse_into_o.therefore: REM-59, REM-60 and REM-61 are three faces of ONE gap: I-14-D's r3 generation was never written. Registered as REM-62.
